title: Professional Motion Graphics & Transitions Knowledge Pack

items.title: Motion Design
items.description: The discipline of designing animated visual communication for brands and interfaces.
definitions: Motion design is the practice of solving communication problems with animated graphics, type, and systems aligned to brand and platform.
Unify style, timing, and hierarchy into a coherent motion language.
rules: Practice: Design stills that animate well
decisionRules: Follow: Design stills that animate well
troubleshooting: Avoid: Inconsistent easing across a brand
examples: Brand open + lower-third system for a campaign
professionalStandards: Motion design is the practice of solving communication problems with animated graphics, type, and systems aligned to brand and platform.

items.title: Motion Graphics Fundamentals
items.description: Building blocks of kinetic graphics: layout, type, shape, and timed reveals.
definitions: Motion graphics fundamentals cover composition, typography in motion, shape language, and basic timing for informational and branded graphics.
Teach readable animated graphics for ads, explainers, and social.
examples: Kinetic list of three benefits with staggered fades
professionalStandards: Motion graphics fundamentals cover composition, typography in motion, shape language, and basic timing for informational and branded graphics.

items.title: Text Animation
items.description: Animating typography for emphasis, rhythm, and readability.
definitions: Text animation is the timed reveal, emphasis, and exit of typographic content that supports voiceover and hierarchy.
Make messages scannable and memorable on mute-heavy platforms.
rules: Practice: Match brand type motion rules
decisionRules: Follow: Match brand type motion rules
troubleshooting: Avoid: Animating faster than reading speed
examples: Word-by-word punch for hook; elegant fade for luxury copy
professionalStandards: Text animation is the timed reveal, emphasis, and exit of typographic content that supports voiceover and hierarchy.

items.title: Logo Animation
items.description: Bringing brand marks to life with controlled, on-brand motion.
definitions: Logo animation is choreographed motion of a brand mark—intros, outros, and stingers—that reinforces identity without distorting the logo’s integrity.
Create recognizable brand punctuation at open/close.
rules: Practice: Keep under a few seconds for social
bestPractices: Keep under a few seconds for social
decisionRules: Follow: Keep under a few seconds for social
recommendations: Keep under a few seconds for social
examples: Stroke draw + settle; 3D light pass then flat lockup
professionalStandards: Logo animation is choreographed motion of a brand mark—intros, outros, and stingers—that reinforces identity without distorting the logo’s integrity.

items.title: Icon Animation
items.description: Micro-motion for icons that clarifies state and delight without noise.
definitions: Icon animation is short, purposeful motion of icons to signal state changes, feedback, or feature highlights.
Improve UI clarity and feature explainers.
examples: Checkmark draw-on; cart icon bounce on add
professionalStandards: Icon animation is short, purposeful motion of icons to signal state changes, feedback, or feature highlights.

items.title: UI Motion
items.description: Interface transitions and feedback motion for products and product videos.
definitions: UI motion is the choreography of interface elements—navigation, feedback, and state—that communicates responsiveness and hierarchy.
Make digital products feel coherent and trustworthy.
troubleshooting: Avoid: Blocking interactions with long animation
examples: Sheet slides up 280ms ease-out; success toast fades
professionalStandards: UI motion is the choreography of interface elements—navigation, feedback, and state—that communicates responsiveness and hierarchy.

items.title: Motion Rhythm
items.description: The patterned timing of moves that creates musical or editorial pulse.
definitions: Motion rhythm is the recurring pattern of accents, holds, and releases that gives a sequence musicality and brand tempo.
Align graphics to music and keep attention through patterned beats.
rules: Practice: Don’t sync every frame literally
decisionRules: Follow: Don’t sync every frame literally
examples: Benefit cards snap on snare hits
professionalStandards: Motion rhythm is the recurring pattern of accents, holds, and releases that gives a sequence musicality and brand tempo.

items.title: Motion Hierarchy
items.description: Ordering what moves first and strongest so attention follows the message.
definitions: Motion hierarchy prioritizes animated elements by amplitude, timing, and contrast so the primary message leads.
Prevent visual competition in dense graphics packages.
examples: Title scales in; supporting icons fade later at lower amplitude
professionalStandards: Motion hierarchy prioritizes animated elements by amplitude, timing, and contrast so the primary message leads.

items.title: Motion Timing
items.description: Duration standards for graphics, UI, and branded motion systems.
definitions: Motion timing for graphics defines duration ranges and easing conventions that keep a brand’s motion language consistent.
Speed craft and consistency across teams and templates.
rules: Practice: Longer for large spatial moves
decisionRules: Follow: Longer for large spatial moves
examples: Brand book: micro 120ms, standard 240ms, expressive 480ms
professionalStandards: Motion timing for graphics defines duration ranges and easing conventions that keep a brand’s motion language consistent.

items.title: Motion Style
items.description: The aesthetic fingerprint of motion—editorial, playful, corporate, cinematic.
definitions: Motion style is the characteristic combination of easing, shape language, texture, and camera behavior that expresses brand personality.
Keep campaigns visually coherent and on-brand.
rules: Practice: Write a motion style frame
decisionRules: Follow: Write a motion style frame
examples: Soft editorial fades vs snappy social pops for same brand tiers
professionalStandards: Motion style is the characteristic combination of easing, shape language, texture, and camera behavior that expresses brand personality.

items.title: Cut
items.description: An instantaneous change from one shot to another—the default editorial transition.
definitions: A cut is an immediate splice between shots with no optical blend, used for clarity, pace, and invisible continuity.
Maintain energy and clarity; the workhorse of professional editing.
rules: Practice: Cut on action when possible
Practice: Prefer cuts unless a blend adds meaning
bestPractices: Prefer cuts unless a blend adds meaning
decisionRules: Follow: Cut on action when possible
Follow: Prefer cuts unless a blend adds meaning
troubleshooting: Avoid: Using fancy transitions as default
recommendations: Prefer cuts unless a blend adds meaning
examples: Action match from pour start to mid-pour angle
professionalStandards: A cut is an immediate splice between shots with no optical blend, used for clarity, pace, and invisible continuity.

items.title: Fade
items.description: Transition to/from black (or a color) signaling time, chapter, or closure.
definitions: A fade gradually changes opacity to or from a solid color, typically black, to indicate passage of time or structural boundaries.
Softly open/close chapters or end films.
examples: Fade from black into brand film; fade out under CTA
professionalStandards: A fade gradually changes opacity to or from a solid color, typically black, to indicate passage of time or structural boundaries.

items.title: Dissolve
items.description: Crossfade between two images suggesting connection or soft time passage.
definitions: A dissolve (crossfade) overlaps the end of one shot with the start of another by blending opacity.
Link ideas gently or compress time without a hard cut.
examples: Morning to night city dissolve; idea A morphs conceptually to B
professionalStandards: A dissolve (crossfade) overlaps the end of one shot with the start of another by blending opacity.

items.title: Wipe
items.description: A geometric leading edge that replaces one shot with another.
definitions: A wipe transitions by a moving boundary (line, clock, iris edge) that reveals the next shot.
Stylized scene changes or chapter markers.
examples: Brand-colored linear wipe into new chapter title
professionalStandards: A wipe transitions by a moving boundary (line, clock, iris edge) that reveals the next shot.

items.title: Match Cut
items.description: A cut that links shots through matched action, shape, or concept.
definitions: A match cut joins two shots by aligning motion, composition, or metaphor so the cut feels continuous or cleverly associative.
Create elegant narrative or visual bridges.
rules: Practice: Serve story not only cleverness
decisionRules: Follow: Serve story not only cleverness
examples: Spinning tire to spinning logo; eye open to sunrise
professionalStandards: A match cut joins two shots by aligning motion, composition, or metaphor so the cut feels continuous or cleverly associative.

items.title: Luma Transition
items.description: Transitions driven by luminance maps or light-based reveals.
definitions: A luma transition uses brightness information—often a gradient or animated matte—to blend or reveal shots.
Create light-motivated, premium graphic transitions.
examples: Light sweep reveal of product from darkness
professionalStandards: A luma transition uses brightness information—often a gradient or animated matte—to blend or reveal shots.

items.title: Shape Transition
items.description: Reveals or morphs using branded shapes and masks.
definitions: A shape transition uses geometric or brand-shaped mattes to reveal the next shot or graphic.
Tie transitions to brand identity systems.
rules: Practice: End clean for next scene
decisionRules: Follow: End clean for next scene
examples: Rounded square expands to full frame like app icon
professionalStandards: A shape transition uses geometric or brand-shaped mattes to reveal the next shot or graphic.

items.title: Zoom Transition
items.description: Scale-based transition that rushes into or out of a subject.
definitions: A zoom transition uses rapid scale (optical or digital) to bridge shots, often with motion blur for energy.
Energetic social pacing or dive into detail.
examples: Snap zoom into product detail then cut wide
professionalStandards: A zoom transition uses rapid scale (optical or digital) to bridge shots, often with motion blur for energy.

items.title: Camera Transition
items.description: Transitions motivated by simulated or real camera moves (whip, push, orbit).
definitions: A camera transition bridges shots using camera-like motion—whip pans, push-ins, or parallax—so the edit feels photographic.
Maintain cinematic continuity between scenes.
rules: Practice: Plan on set when possible
decisionRules: Follow: Plan on set when possible
examples: Whip pan from lifestyle to studio hero
professionalStandards: A camera transition bridges shots using camera-like motion—whip pans, push-ins, or parallax—so the edit feels photographic.

items.title: Creative Transitions
items.description: Custom, concept-driven transitions unique to a campaign’s visual idea.
definitions: Creative transitions are bespoke transitional devices—morphs, object wipes, or graphic gags—designed for a specific narrative or brand concept.
Make signature moments memorable when budget and concept support them.
rules: Practice: Don’t invent one per cut
decisionRules: Follow: Don’t invent one per cut
examples: Product lid closes as wipe; ink bleed morph between scenes
professionalStandards: Creative transitions are bespoke transitional devices—morphs, object wipes, or graphic gags—designed for a specific narrative or brand concept.
